answer: On September 15, 2026, the Board of Supervisors voted 7-4 to finally pass an ordinance amending several municipal codes regarding street tree standards, in-lieu fees for development projects, accessory dwelling unit (ADU) exemptions, and appeals concerning the removal of hazardous trees. Supervisors Connie Chan, Jackie Fielder, Bilal Sauter, and Shamann Walton voted against the measure.

bullets.text: The Board finally passed an ordinance amending the Public Works, Administrative, Planning, and Business and Tax Regulations Codes regarding street tree standards, development in-lieu fees, ADU exemptions, and hazardous tree removal appeals on a 7-4 vote, with Supervisors Chan, Fielder, Sauter, and Walton dissenting.
bullets.item_title: Public Works, Administrative, Planning, Business and Tax Regulations Codes - Street Tree Standards, Appeals, and Adopt-A-Tree Fund

rows.item_title: 1 ROLL CALL AND PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE
rows.summary: The Board of Supervisors called the meeting to order and established a quorum with all eleven members present. Board President Mandelman read the land acknowledgment of the Ramaytush Ohlone and led the Pledge of Allegiance.

rows.item_title: 3 SPECIAL ORDER 2:00 P.M. - Mayor’s Appearance Before The Board[Mayor Appearance Boiler 01-2013|B1,B2]
rows.summary: Mayor Daniel Lurie addressed the Board during the 2:00 p.m. special order regarding the city's housing affordability crisis and rising eviction numbers. He highlighted proposed tenant protection legislation, rental assistance investments, housing production initiatives through Permit SF, and early labor agreements reached with municipal employee unions. The matter was discussed and filed.

rows.item_title: 2 COMMUNICATIONS
rows.summary: The Clerk announced communications regarding options for in-person attendance at City Hall and live broadcasting on SFGovTV. Instructions were also provided for submitting written public comments and requesting disability accommodations.

rows.item_title: 3 APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES
rows.summary: The Board considered the approval of meeting minutes from July 21, July 28, and September 1, 2026. The minutes were approved unanimously on a roll call vote.

rows.item_title: Items 1 through 15
rows.summary: The Board took up Items 1 through 15 on the consent agenda. The ordinances were passed on first reading and resolutions adopted unanimously by roll call vote without objection.

rows.item_title: Public Works, Administrative, Planning, Business and Tax Regulations Codes - Street Tree Standards, Appeals, and Adopt-A-Tree Fund
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending multiple municipal codes relating to street tree standards, in-lieu fees for development projects, ADU exemptions, and appeals of hazardous tree removals. The ordinance was finally passed on a 7-4 vote, with Supervisors Chan, Fielder, Sauter, and Walton dissenting.

rows.item_title: Authorizing Tax-Exempt and/or Taxable Certificates of Participation - Open Space Fund - Not to Exceed $43,000,000
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance authorizing the issuance and sale of Certificates of Participation not to exceed $43 million for the Open Space Fund to finance and refinance capital projects. The ordinance was approved on first reading by unanimous roll call vote.

rows.item_title: Appropriation - Certificates of Participation Series 2026A, Open Space Fund - Recreation and Park Proceeds - Recreation and Park - $43,000,000
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance appropriating $43 million of Certificates of Participation Series 2026A proceeds for the Open Space Fund to the Recreation and Park Department for fiscal year 2026-2027. The measure was approved on first reading by unanimous roll call vote.

rows.item_title: Sale of General Obligation Bonds (Social Bonds - Affordable Housing, 2019), Series 2026D - Not to Exceed $107,540,000
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $107,540,000 in general obligation social bonds for affordable housing under the 2019 bond program. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Appropriation - General Obligation Bond Proceeds - $202,004,550 - MOHCD - Affordable Housing Series 2026D, Affordable Housing Series 2026E, Preservation and Seismic Safety Series 2026F - FY2026-2027
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance appropriating $202,004,550 in general obligation bond proceeds to the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development for fiscal year 2026-2027. The funding supports middle-income, senior, low-income, and seismic safety affordable housing projects. The ordinance was passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Sale of General Obligation Bonds (Health and Recovery, 2020), Series 2026B - Not to Exceed $83,475,000
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $83,475,000 in general obligation bonds for the 2020 Health and Recovery program. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: De-Appropriation - DPH - General Obligation Bond Proceeds - 2020 Health and Recovery, Series 2025G - $43,505,000 - Appropriation - DPH and REC - General Obligation Bond Proceeds - 2020 Health and Recovery, Series 2026B - $83,475,000 - FY2026-2027
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance de-appropriating $43.5 million from Series 2025G and appropriating $83,475,000 from Series 2026B Health and Recovery bond proceeds to the Department of Public Health and Recreation and Parks Department. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Sale of General Obligation Bonds (Earthquake Safety and Emergency Response, 2020), Series 2026C - Not to Exceed $138,000,000
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing the issuance and sale of up to $138 million in general obligation bonds for Earthquake Safety and Emergency Response. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Appropriation - General Obligation Bond Proceeds - $138,000,000 - Earthquake Safety and Emergency Response, Series 2026C - DPW - FY2026-2027
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance appropriating $138 million of Earthquake Safety and Emergency Response bond proceeds to the Department of Public Works for fiscal year 2026-2027. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Professional Services Agreement Modification - AtkinsRéalis USA Inc. - Project Management Support Services - Airfield Improvement Program, 2024-2029 Phase - Not to Exceed $17,000,000
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution approving a contract modification with AtkinsRéalis USA Inc. for airfield project management support services at San Francisco International Airport. The modification increases the contract by $8.4 million to a total of $17 million through February 2029. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Accept and Expend Grant - Retroactive - San Francisco Health Plan - San Francisco Health Plan Community Health Assessment/Community Health Improvement Plan Grant - $204,313.34
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution retroactively authorizing the Department of Public Health to accept and expend an approximate $204,000 grant from the San Francisco Health Plan for the Community Health Assessment and Improvement Plan. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Grant Agreement - Retroactive - 1166 Howard Street Associates, LP - Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund and Program - Not to Exceed $3,239,075
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing a retroactive grant agreement with 1166 Howard Street Associates, LP for up to $3,239,075 through December 2042. The grant provides project-based rental subsidies for an 88-unit 100% affordable housing development. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Grant Agreement - Retroactive - MHDC South Park Properties, LP - Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund and Program - Amount Not to Exceed $3,798,723
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing a retroactive grant agreement with MHDC South Park Properties, LP for up to $3,798,723 through December 2043. The agreement provides project-based rental subsidies for a 160-unit affordable housing development under the Affordable Housing Opportunity Fund. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: 7 SPECIAL ORDER 2:30 P.M. - Recognition of Commendations
rows.summary: Supervisors presented commendations recognizing various individuals and groups for meritorious service to San Francisco. Honorees included participants in the Department of Public Health's Living Proof campaign, Recreation and Parks Commission President Kat Anderson, SFPD Commander Christopher Delgado, SFFD NERT volunteers, Joanne Giovannoni of Portal World Travel, KTSF Channel 26 on its 50th anniversary, and members of the Castro Public Works Block Sweepers team.

rows.item_title: Hearing - Committee of the Whole - Infrastructure Financing Plan Annexation Supplement - San Francisco Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 1 (Treasure Island) - September 15, 2026, at 3:00 p.m.
rows.summary: The Board convened as a Committee of the Whole to hold a public hearing on adding territory and adopting an annexation supplement for Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 1 on Treasure Island. Staff from the Treasure Island Development Authority presented the plan components and bonding capacity. No public comments were received, and the hearing was closed and filed.

rows.item_title: Adding Territory - Adopting Annexation Supplement - Amended and Restated Infrastructure Financing Plan -Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 1 (Treasure Island)
rows.summary: The Board considered Items 42 and 43 to approve adding territory to the Treasure Island Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District and calling a special landowner election. Both resolutions were adopted unanimously by roll call vote.

rows.item_title: Modifying Resolution No. 7-17 - Authorize Issuance of Bonds - Infrastructure and Revitalization Financing District No. 1 (Treasure Island)
rows.summary: The Board considered Items 44 through 46 relating to declaring landowner election results, adding territory, and modifying bond authorizations for the Treasure Island IRFD. On a motion by Supervisor Dorsey, the Board voted without objection to continue the items to September 29, 2026.

rows.item_title: Contract Agreement - OpenGov Inc. - Permitting Software Product Agreement - Not to Exceed $38,965,985.92
rows.summary: The Board considered an amendment to the OpenGov Inc. contract for citywide permitting software. Supervisor Chyanne Chen introduced amendments reducing the extension from five to three years and reducing the contract total from $38.9 million to $28 million with added oversight provisions. The amendment passed without objection, and the resolution as amended was adopted on a 10-1 vote, with Supervisor Fielder dissenting.

rows.item_title: Administrative Code - Amended Airport Surveillance Technology Policy
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance approving the amended Airport Surveillance Technology Policy governing third-party security camera use at SFO. The ordinance passed on first reading by unanimous roll call vote.

rows.item_title: Settlement of Lawsuit - Gabriel Shin - $6,000,000
rows.summary: The Board considered ordinances authorizing settlements of two employment dispute lawsuits against the City, including the Gabriel Shin matter for $6 million and the Quirolgico Arroyo et al. matter for $8.7 million. Both ordinances were passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Presidential Appointment, Planning Commission - Malea Chavez
rows.summary: The Board considered a motion to approve Board President Mandelman's nomination of Malea Chavez to the Planning Commission for a term ending July 1, 2028. Supervisor Melgar spoke in strong support of Chavez's community background and collaborative approach. The motion was approved without objection.

rows.item_title: City Controller Appointment, Sanitation and Streets Commission - Christopher Simi
rows.summary: The Board considered City Controller Greg Wagner's nomination of Christopher Simi to the Sanitation and Streets Commission for a term ending July 1, 2030. The motion approving the appointment was passed without objection.

rows.item_title: 9 ROLL CALL FOR INTRODUCTIONS [Roll Call Boiler|B1, B2]
rows.summary: Supervisors introduced new legislation and provided committee updates during roll call for introductions. Key proposals included an OpenGov oversight hearing, tenant notices on state rent caps, behested payment reporting, a resolution condemning SFO immigration detention, shelter dog safety rules, storefront transparency exemptions for bathhouses, co-op housing support, street repaving bike network rules, banked rent increase caps, official misconduct charges for a sheriff oversight commissioner, an interim zoning moratorium on data centers, and micromobility regulations.

rows.item_title: 10 PUBLIC COMMENT [Public Comment Boiler|B1, B2, N1]
rows.summary: The Board heard general public comment on a variety of local issues. Members of the public voiced concerns regarding street conditions, drug dealing, and open-air drug use in the Hub neighborhood, demands for regulation and bans on artificial intelligence and data centers, concerns regarding workplace discrimination against Black city workers, and heartfelt tributes to the late youth activist Felicia 'Opie' Freeney with calls to close Juvenile Hall.

rows.item_title: 12 FOR ADOPTION WITHOUT COMMITTEE REFERENCE[For Adoption Boiler|B1,B2]
rows.summary: The Board considered Items 51 through 59 on the agenda for adoption without committee reference, severing Items 52 and 58 for individual consideration. The remaining resolutions and motions were adopted on a 10-0 roll call vote, with Supervisor Chan absent.

rows.item_title: Muni Heritage Weekend - September 2026
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution declaring September 19-20, 2026, as Muni Heritage Weekend in San Francisco. Supervisor Dorsey spoke on the 113-year history of the Municipal Railway, celebrated public transit workers, and invited the community to upcoming museum events. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Latin@ Heritage Month - September 15 through October 15, 2026
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution declaring September 15 through October 15, 2026, as Latin@ Heritage Month in San Francisco. Supervisors Melgar and Fielder spoke on the rich cultural heritage and resilience of the Latino community in San Francisco. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: 14 ADJOURNMENT
rows.summary: The Board adjourned the meeting in memory of Felicia 'Opie' Freeney, Jeremiah Halsey, Thomas 'Tom' Frankel, and Mayling Zhu Low.
